method: Whole-file manual reading of ProcessWatcher.cs and SettingsManager.cs; exact-commit download bytes matched pinned Git blob IDs. No process hooks or settings mutation executed.
findings: Process watcher skips overlapping scans using Monitor.TryEnter, polls at minimum100ms and tracks PID plus Process object/session. HasExited exceptions are treated as termination, conflating inaccessible/inconsistent observation with actual exit.

Dispose stops/disposes timer but does not acquire scan lock or wait in-flight callbacks. Scan admission checks disposed only before locking, so callbacks can continue enumerating/adding after disposal begins. Source-level race, not reproduced runtime outcome.
Exited event enabled before dictionary insertion can race fast termination; later scans may recover via HasExited. Failed TryAdd does not explicitly unsubscribe/dispose new Process instance.

Events posted to captured SynchronizationContext may run after disposal; callback exceptions occur later outside posting caller catch. Without context, ProcessCreated handler exception is caught as process handling failure after insertion, potentially retaining a disposed tracked object.

Settings serializes directly via File.WriteAllText to main settings path without temp/replace, backup or durability barrier. Write failures are only Debug logged; setters already mutate memory and some emit change events despite persistence failure.

Settings load catches read/parse failures and uses defaults, but directory creation precedes that catch and can fail static initialization. No file-size limit, locking, schema version or explicit corruption diagnostic present.
ClosedWindows array and other settings are mutable references without internal synchronization. These utility preferences are not a transactional duplicate-index/cache design.
limits: No Windows process lifecycle, timer-race fault injection, settings durability tests or original suite executed. No foreign production code adopted.
Full filtered checkout remains separate session13181; individually retrieved source is pinned. Completed count148/500; pHash deferred.
